@graph.name: Shopify product exporter
@graph.description: Export the full product catalogue of any Shopify store to CSV: titles, prices, variants, SKUs, images and SEO metas. Free, no sign-up, ready to import.
featureList: File in the Shopify import format

mainEntity.name: What is a Shopify product exporter?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is a tool that reads the public product feed of a Shopify storefront and turns it into a downloadable file. Instead of copying titles, prices and image links product by product, you get the whole catalogue in one CSV, structured the way Shopify's own product import expects it.

mainEntity.name: Can I export products from any Shopify store?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, as long as the store publishes its catalogue, which is the default on Shopify. A store that has closed its product feed, or that sits behind a password, returns nothing and the tool says so. You never need to own or have access to the store.
Yes, with no credit card and no trial period. It is one of the free tools Copyfy publishes alongside the theme detector and the subscription calculator.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a Shopify account to use it?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The tool reads the storefront the same way a browser does, so no Shopify login, no API key and no app install are involved. You only need a Shopify account on the receiving side, when you import the file into your own store.

mainEntity.name: What data fields are included in the export?

acceptedAnswer.text: Product title, handle, HTML description, vendor, type and tags. Then every variant with its option values, price, compare-at price, SKU, weight, shipping requirement and tax status. Then every image URL with its position and alt text, plus the variant image. Finally the meta title and meta description read from the live product page.

mainEntity.name: What file format do I get?

acceptedAnswer.text: A CSV encoded in UTF-8 with a byte order mark, which means accented characters display correctly when you open it in Excel, Numbers or Google Sheets. The CSV is deliberate rather than a limitation: Shopify's product import only accepts CSV, so a spreadsheet format would break the one thing that matters here.

mainEntity.name: How long does the export take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A small catalogue of a few dozen products is done in a couple of seconds. A catalogue of 2000 products takes around twenty seconds without the metas option. Collecting meta titles, meta descriptions and alt text means reading each product page, so it adds time in proportion to the catalogue size; a progress bar shows where the tool is.

mainEntity.name: Is there a limit on the number of products I can export?

acceptedAnswer.text: The export stops at 2000 products. When a catalogue is larger, the file still downloads and a message tells you it was capped, so you never assume you got everything.

Yes, every image of every product, in position order and with its alt text when the store filled one in. The file carries the image URLs rather than the image files, which is exactly what the Shopify importer wants: it downloads each image from the source store during the import.

Yes, with the store's own option names, so a catalogue built on size and colour keeps those two axes. Each variant gets its own row, with its price, compare-at price, SKU and weight, plus its dedicated image when the store assigned one.

mainEntity.name: How is this different from Shopify's native export?

acceptedAnswer.text: The native export only works on a store you own or have staff access to, and it reaches back-office fields like inventory quantities, barcodes and cost per item. This tool works on any storefront without an account, but only sees what the storefront publishes. They cover opposite needs rather than competing.

mainEntity.name: Can I use this for dropshipping product research?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it is the most common use. Exporting a competitor's catalogue shows their full range, their price ladder and how deep their variants go, in one table instead of dozens of page visits. Pair it with an ad spy to tell the products a store merely lists from the products it actually pushes.

Yes. Every export reads the storefront at the moment you run it, so prices and product lists reflect the store as it stands. Nothing is served from a stored copy, which also means two exports run a week apart will legitimately differ.

mainEntity.name: Can I export from a password-protected Shopify store?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A store under password protection serves nothing publicly, and the tool does not try to get around that. The same goes for a store that has deliberately closed its product feed. In both cases you get a clear message rather than an empty file.

mainEntity.name: How do I import the exported file into another Shopify store?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the destination store, open Products, click Import, and drop the CSV. Shopify reads the 42 columns, creates the products with their variants, and downloads the images from their URLs. Inventory tracking is left empty in the file so the products arrive sellable rather than out of stock; set your own stock afterwards if you track it.
